name: Zimbabwe

findings.summary: State-owned TelOne began a Huawei-supplied national broadband upgrade covering exchanges, core network, backbone links and billing, funded by a roughly US$98.6 million China Exim Bank facility; Huawei was awarded the contract in 2010.
findings.analyst_inference: Tier 4: financing drawn (US$33m by March 2017 per DCD) and phase one under way; completion not confirmed in this pass. Pre-2020 finding; current status not checked (still_current null).

findings.summary: TelOne opened two colocation and cloud data centres in Harare and Mazowe, developed with Huawei under the first phase of the Exim-financed national broadband project, at a reported cost of US$1.6 million.
findings.analyst_inference: Owner-operator TelOne is Zimbabwean state-owned, so domestic; Huawei recorded as builder. Huawei's exact role (construction vs IT equipment) not specified; if Huawei supplies and maintains the IT stack, an equipment finding would be prc. Small facilities; pre-2020, still_current null.

findings.summary: Huawei's NetOne mobile network upgrade, announced in July 2013 and cut from US$298.6 million to about US$218 million, was approved by the State Procurement Board despite overpricing concerns and a court challenge; Exim Bank financing was envisaged.
findings.analyst_inference: Single opened S2 source. Tier 3 on SPB approval; whether the contract was executed at the reduced value and the outcome of the court challenge were not established. Pre-2020; still_current null.

findings.summary: NetOne signed a US$71 million agreement with Huawei Technologies International for network expansion and modernisation, including about 250 rural base stations in the first 100 days.
findings.analyst_inference: Described as a funding agreement; lender not named. Global Voices (2023) says NetOne was upgrading to 4G/5G with Huawei; DCD (2024) says NetOne's 5G vendor was unconfirmed, so 5G vendor is not coded. Econet's RAN/core vendor not found.

findings.summary: Zimbabwe's government agreed with Guangzhou-based CloudWalk on a mass facial-recognition programme reportedly extending to transport hubs and a national facial database, with face data shared to train CloudWalk's systems; reported on hold pending 2018 elections.
findings.analyst_inference: Tier 2: cooperation agreement with no disclosed value or contract terms. Foreign Policy partly relays a PRC state outlet (Science and Technology Daily) on scope. Implementation after 2018 unconfirmed; Global Voices (2023) alleges CloudWalk holds voter-registration biometrics, not independently verified. still_current null.

findings.summary: Advocacy reporting says Huawei leads a police surveillance grid under a reported US$100 million contract running to 2025, with US$20 million spent in a first tranche in 2020, and CloudWalk and Hikvision supplying facial recognition.
findings.analyst_inference: Only one opened source, itself secondary; ADF is US-military-affiliated (S4) and unopened. Contract counterparty and value unverified; tier 3 is provisional. Global Voices also reports Hikvision facial recognition at airports and border posts (not coded separately).

findings.controller: Unnamed Chinese firm (Hikvision per Techzim commentary)
findings.summary: President Mnangagwa reportedly approved a Chinese company installing night-vision surveillance cameras on some Harare streets to curb road accidents and crime.
findings.analyst_inference: Vendor identity inferred: Techzim's commentary names Hikvision but its news summary does not; NewsDay original not opened. Tier 1 (approval only, no contract). Scale subnational (one city). Pre-2020; still_current null.

findings.summary: President Mnangagwa commissioned a National Data Centre in Harare, built in partnership with the Chinese government, to link databases of state institutions and economic actors.
findings.analyst_inference: Single opened S3 source; builder, financier and IT-equipment vendor not named, so builder left null despite reported Chinese partnership. If a PRC vendor supplies and operates the IT stack, a prc equipment finding would apply.

findings.summary: Econet launched a dedicated AI unit offering customers six months' free access to Google Gemini from May 2026, alongside Cassava AiCloud compute on Nvidia GPUs hosted at Cassava's AI Factory in South Africa.
findings.analyst_inference: Model used via Google's service, so us pole. Tier 3 assumes a commercial distribution agreement; terms not disclosed. Nvidia compute sits outside Zimbabwe, so no silicon finding. Cassava and Econet are Strive Masiyiwa-linked; Cassava's AI Factory is in South Africa.

silicon.null_reason: no accelerator deployments in Zimbabwe found; Cassava/Nvidia GPUs used by Econet are hosted in South Africa (1 search)

power.null_reason: no AI- or data-centre-specific power evidence surfaced

research_gaps: Who supplies Econet Wireless's RAN and core (Econet launched 5G in 2022), and NetOne's 5G vendor?
Was the 2013 Huawei-NetOne upgrade executed, at what value, and how did the Muguti court challenge end? Lender for the 2017 US$71m deal?
Primary evidence (procurement, budget lines) for the reported US$100m Huawei police surveillance contract and its status after 2025.
Did the 2018 CloudWalk facial-recognition programme proceed, and is it still in use?
Builder, financier and equipment vendor of the 2021 National Data Centre in Harare.
Any PRC-built submarine/terrestrial cable or HMN Tech involvement; any Zimbabwean government adoption of a frontier model.
